content.title: NCAA Wrestling Championships 2026 FREE STREAM: How to watch finals on Day 3
content.text: If you purchase a product through a link on our site, we may receive compensation.CLEVELAND, Ohio – Penn State is closing in on a historic 5-peat as 10 individual champions are crowned in Cleveland for the final day of the 2026 Division I NCAA Wrestling Championships today – Saturday, March 21 – at Rocket Arena. There are multiple free streaming options to watch this finale.How do I watch the NCAA Wrestling Championships for free? The 2026 NCAA Wrestling Championships conclude today at 10 a.m. Eastern with Session 5 on ESPNU. Session 6 will take place on ESPN at 6 p.m. You can catch all the action at no cost by utilizing a free trial from FuboTV ($25 off first month) or DIRECTV, which offers a free trial and $35 off your first month. Sling TV is the most flexible option. The streaming service now offers new users a Day Pass for $4.99, Weekend Pass for $9.99, Week Pass for $14.99, Monthly for $45.99 and Season Pass for $199.99 for five months and $45.99 per month thereafter. Pair the Orange and Blue package together and receive half off your first month at $29.99. Note: In order to watch Session 5 with ESPNU on Sling TV, you will need the Sling Day Pass ($4.99) with the Sports Extra add-on ($1). The entire 2026 NCAA Wrestling Championships, including an all-encompassing MATCAST, will broadcast live on the ESPN app streaming service, which now offers an Unlimited Plan for $29.99 per month (or $299.99 for entire year) and the Select Plan for $12.99 per month (or $129.99 for entire year).Today’s wrestling schedule Saturday March 21SESSION 5Session 5 begins at 10 a.m. Eastern on ESPNU and ESPN Streaming with Wrestle-Back semifinals and third, fifth and seventh place medal round matches.SESSION 6Session 6 begins at 6 p.m. Eastern on ESPN and ESPN Streaming with championship weight class finals and individual weight class awards. After entering the tournament with a school-record seven No. 1 seeds, and finishing 6-2 in the semifinals, four-time defending national champion Penn State will take an NCAA-record tying six wrestlers into the finals to compete for a national championship. Luke Lilledahl (125), Shayne Van Ness (149), Mitchell Mesenbrink (165), Levi Haines (174), Rocco Welsh (184) and Josh Barr (197) will wrestle to become champions of their weight class in 2026. Marcus Blaze (133) and PJ Duke (157) both lost their semifinals. The Nittany Lions have run away with the team score race, tallying 153 points. The next closest team is Oklahoma State with 104.5. Penn State is in prime position to break their own record for the most points in the NCAA Championships with 177 last year. Looking for more info?
